files.summary: Respells MANIFEST_SCHEMA from VSTD-PAGES-DEPLOYMENT-MANIFEST-1 to verifier-pages-deployment-manifest-1 and raises MAX_FILE_BYTES from 8 to 32 mebibytes, which a source comment ties to MAX_PACKAGE_BYTES in verifier.interoperability.storage; the bound applies to each manifest-listed file size and to each live route fetch, while MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES stays 8 mebibytes, MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES 4 mebibytes and MAX_TOTAL_BYTES 64 mebibytes.

The live receipt states that every manifest-listed live route and the manifest itself matched the exact bounded bytes at observation time; future availability and future bytes are not established.

files.summary: Checks pull-request scope and exact changed-source coverage across a digest-bound manifest and optional inline rows; local pre-push may explicitly accept a pending hosted run.
files.limits: Hosted validation remains strict, and structural coverage plus authored summaries does not prove behavioral correctness.

files.summary: Compares description words using str.split: before a push, the supplied or live description is compared with the revision in force at the current head's first recorded pull-request workflow run; after a push, --pushed compares revisions in force at that head's inferred push and the latest earlier recorded head push. Spacing-only edits do not count. A first recorded push passes without an earlier comparison; with earlier history, an unedited description is unrevised. Recorded revised comparisons exit 0, unrevised comparisons 1.
files.limits: Push times are inferred from first pull-request workflow-run timestamps; unobserved heads are not recorded. An absent recorded head-push timestamp or a missing/deleted applicable historical revision raises Unanswered; a never-edited description is unrevised when a comparison is required. The command reports these refusals and unrevised comparisons as FAIL with exit 1. Word changes do not establish description correctness, comprehension, implementation qualification or publication authority.

files.summary: Requires a Test skip rubric disclosure section in the pull-request body with a Skipped test inventory table of four-column rows. Under a DISCLOSED test disposition the table is nonempty and each row names one of eight rubric categories that is also checked in the rubric checklist, with a technical reason and a claim consequence; every checked category is itemized by some row and NOT_APPLICABLE is unchecked. Under the NONE test disposition (no test skipped) NOT_APPLICABLE is checked, no category is checked and no row names a rubric category. The parsed disclosure (test_skip_rubric) now joins the promotion record, so the record SHA-256 covers it, and validate reports it in its PASS receipt. The ninth REQUIRED_CHECKLIST_ITEMS entry now reads that every skipped test is categorized under the formal skip rubric with technical rationale, or verified zero skips. Counts the logits-constraints report among the thirteen expected hosted pytest reports. The accepted marker line is now acceptance-clearance, not VSTD-HUMAN-ACCEPTANCE, and the unchecked-item scan now covers only the Checklist section.
files.limits: The check proves only that required evidence is complete and that a trusted repository participant accepted the exact record digest and head; it cannot prove comprehension, correctness, independence, merge authority, or release authority. Skip reasons and claim consequences are screened for emptiness and placeholder words such as N/A, NONE, TODO, TBD, PENDING and REPLACE, not judged for truth. Inventory rows are not matched to the individual skips recorded in the test-evidence manifest.

files.summary: Checks one closed, source-bound PRDEL native-v2 development-candidate inventory for exact path, role, status, limits, byte length and SHA-256 digest, including the unchanged historical manifest-v2 boundary.
files.limits: Byte admission does not execute PRDEL, authenticate tests, establish semantic completeness, or authorize release. The sealed aggregate coordinate is externally selected rather than recomputed by this checker.

files.summary: Checks the exact PRDEL native-v2 implementation coordinate, externally selected release subject, local base/head history, selected source bytes, and production description-gate result.
files.limits: A valid coordinate is not semantic completeness, hosted-run evidence, human acceptance, publication authority, or a release decision; absent host selection remains UNKNOWN.

files.summary: Runs repository presentation checks over declared documentation, acronyms and release-facing text.
files.limits: Presentation checks do not establish code correctness or release authorization.

files.summary: Selects the documentation pin for installation commands separately from the unreleased source version (an UNRELEASED changelog entry makes installation pins, including the verifier.__version__ output-comment check, use the previous dated release, and an unreleased candidate without one is an error); reports a company-site or ClaimGarden directory that holds neither expected file as NOT_FOUND instead of OBSERVED; reports an absent hero badge or metric card as a missing-version action item instead of failing on the missing field; and a clean report names the surfaces it did not observe.
files.limits: Selecting the documentation pin is not evidence of external publication. Unless --offline is given the check makes one HTTPS request to the PyPI JSON endpoint (timeout 4.0 seconds), and without --target-sync it judges the estate pages against the version PyPI reports, or against the target version when PyPI reports none, so its result depends on a live index and on operator-named estate directories. The company-site and ClaimGarden pages are read from local directories and no deployed site is fetched, so deployed synchronization is not established.

files.summary: Scans selected release artifacts for prohibited text patterns without echoing matched content.
files.limits: A pattern scan is bounded by its inputs and rules and cannot prove absence of every sensitive datum.

files.limits: Those two path prefixes are excluded from this prose gate. It tests only its registered phrase patterns; it does not verify runtime semantics or rename public compatibility identifiers.

files.summary: Reads exact caller-selected relative member bytes after validating the path and parent chain.
files.limits: The adapter does not discover members or establish authority for their selection.

files.summary: Supplies a bounded fixture for exact source-scope binding tests.
files.limits: The fixture covers only its declared source scope and does not authenticate an application-wide denominator.

files.summary: Extends the existing direct-execution import of the release-version classifier (classify_release_version) with a nested fallback: when the bare import raises ModuleNotFoundError, the resolved directory of this script is inserted at the front of sys.path and the import is retried once, so a second failure still propagates. The script otherwise extracts the nonempty body under the one changelog heading that carries the exact version and a YYYY-MM-DD shaped date, and exits with status 1 and a RELEASE NOTES INVALID message on stderr for an unsupported version, a heading count other than one, an empty body or an unreadable changelog.
files.limits: The nested fallback only prepends the script directory to sys.path and retries one import; it does not create a release, validate upstream publication or check that a heading date is a real calendar date.

files.summary: Retains selected Tier-4 native case seeds with bound requests, policies and encoded evidence.
files.limits: Seed data does not execute or register its cases and does not establish Tier-4 conformance.

files.summary: Provides the statically discoverable command wrapper for the installed package manifest migration engine.
files.limits: The wrapper does not itself select reasons, certify migration, or authorize publication.

files.summary: Provides the current documentation portal home template with explicitly substituted release and root-link tokens.
files.limits: Template markup does not publish a site or prove the linked behavior.

files.summary: Labels each documentation search result with its edition as 'Released 1.5.0 archive' or 'v2.0.0 candidate source' instead of 'Released package' or 'Repository source'.
files.limits: Label text only: search, indexing and the edition split are unchanged, and a label does not establish that either edition is deployed.

files.summary: Provides a release documentation home template with renderer-selected release and link tokens.
files.limits: Rendering or retaining a template does not establish a published release.

files.limits: Local preflight is not the hosted run, and pending does not count as a completed repository check.

files.summary: Prepares deterministic release-bound platform evidence from selected hosted artifact inputs.
files.limits: Prepared evidence does not itself execute hosted checks or authorize release.

files.summary: Supplies the Windows-specific anchored-member fixture used by exact-path tests.
files.limits: The fixture is platform-scoped and does not establish cross-platform conformance or release readiness.

files.summary: Sets package version to 2.0.0 and lazily exports grounded and domain certification APIs. The version advances to the unreleased 2.0.0 release candidate; lazy exports are preserved.
files.limits: A package version and exports are not evidence of a published release or complete VSTD conformance.

files.summary: Delegates python -m verifier to the public CLI entry point.
files.limits: The module defines no command behavior of its own; it calls the same main as the vstd and verifier console entry points, which require the package to have been installed. From a source checkout it is documented to work with PYTHONPATH=src.

files.summary: Artifact freeze, seal and thaw module. FREEZE_SCHEMA, SEAL_SCHEMA, SEAL_PAYLOAD_SCHEMA, THAW_SCHEMA and CANONICALIZATION change from their VSTD-ARTIFACT spellings to verifier-artifact-freeze-1, verifier-artifact-seal-1, verifier-artifact-seal-closure-1, verifier-artifact-thaw-1 and verifier-artifact-canonical-1. Existing vstd- record prefixes, vstd-reference-freezer and .vstd-thaw.json remain. _verify_seal delegates public-key admission to imported admit_ed25519_public_key before backend verification, converts either ValueError or InvalidSignature into ArtifactControlError, and verify_frozen_artifact increments invalid_seals when that error is caught.
files.limits: A valid seal establishes only artifact identity and closure under declared mechanisms, not correctness, freshness, ownership, authorization or actor reputation. Former schema strings are not migrated: freeze, seal and thaw version checks and freeze mechanism equality refuse them. CANONICALIZATION is part of the artifact/content descriptor hash input. The key-screen algorithm itself is outside this named file.

files.summary: Declares oneOf shapes for freeze manifests, self-closing seal envelopes and thaw lineage records, with additionalProperties:false and verifier-artifact-freeze-1, verifier-artifact-seal-1, verifier-artifact-seal-closure-1 and verifier-artifact-thaw-1 constants. The freeze canonicalization is verifier-artifact-canonical-1; identifiers carry SHA-256 and SHA3-256 patterns, and thaw requires selected parent identifiers.
files.limits: The schema states that shape-valid thaw metadata does not verify a parent or historical copy and that established clean or dirty status requires verification against the actual sealed parent. These are mechanism formats, not receipts or numbered-profile conformance. Public-key/signature fields are strings with base64 contentEncoding; this schema implements no signature verification.

files.summary: Package facade that re-exports eight names from the engine module of the same package: the types ConsentContext, ConsentEvaluation, ConsentKey, ConsentPolicy and ConsentVerdict and the functions authenticate_consent, evaluate_consent and recheck_consent, all listed in __all__. The package docstring calls them proposed level-7 consent admission mechanisms.
files.limits: The docstring states that consent admission never changes a computational verdict and refers to CONSENT_LEVEL7.md. The file only re-exports names from the engine module and contains no logic of its own.

files.summary: Evaluates authenticated exact-scope consent against externally configured roots, revocation status, caller context, policy and time. Captures bounded plain evidence and trusted inputs before authentication, interpretation or receipt emission; rejects subtype membership/length deception, malformed clocks, oversized fields and deep candidate data without uncaptured receipt serialization. Shares captured native admission rules through an internal fixed-authenticator seam; the public evaluation selects the shared-secret authenticator and the verifier-consent-grant-1 and verifier-consent-revocations-1 wire versions. Missing or stale evidence or trusted inputs give UNKNOWN; any refuted check gives REJECTED. authenticate_consent builds the keyed envelope for a grant or status body; recheck_consent reruns the evaluation and compares every receipt field.
files.limits: Local admission under caller-selected symmetric roots only; no legal authority, execution permission, person authentication or computational correctness. Capture is not atomic against arbitrary concurrent runtime mutation. Trusted secret length has a minimum, not a finite upper operator-resource budget. The file states that an authenticated statement is a configured shared-key statement, not human consent, legal authority, public-key attribution or computational validity; no authorization is enforced (the receipt carries enforcement NOT_ESTABLISHED), no underlying computation is rerun and the carried computational_verdict is caller input.

files.summary: Selects bounded public-key authority with separate grant and revocation key roles, artifact bindings and a chain limit of 1–16. It delegates key screening to signature_keys.admit_ed25519_public_key, verifies exact domain-separated Ed25519 envelope bytes through an optional backend, and delegates grant/revocation admission to native._evaluate_authenticated with the public grant/status wire versions. It rechecks complete receipt bytes under independently selected context, policy, evidence, time and computational verdict; exact replay can reproduce PASS, UNKNOWN or REJECTED, while unavailable checking can yield UNAVAILABLE.
files.limits: A signature establishes a configured-key statement only. Human consent, holder authority, registry completeness, clock authenticity and enforcement remain external; enforcement is NOT_ESTABLISHED and no operation is performed. The computational verdict is caller input. Key screening does not verify signatures or prove secure key generation. Missing cryptographic capability yields UNKNOWN; known bindings/signature contradictions reject. Reproduction is not admission.

files.summary: Evaluates separate stages 7.1 terminal action scope, 7.2 configured root/key/artifact authority, 7.3 time and authenticated revocation freshness, 7.4 nonwidening acyclic delegation with authority/validity prerequisites, and 7.6 consent-result noninterference across all five computational verdicts. Authentication delegates to public._authenticate. FAIL dominates UNKNOWN in stage admission. The 7.5 rechecker binds the exact selected context/policy/evidence/time/verdict and all stage fields; it distinguishes REPRODUCED/PASS reproduction, unavailable checking/UNKNOWN and contradiction/FAIL, while reporting admission separately.
files.limits: The primitives do not register namespace objectives, establish all required holders, authenticate clocks or establish voluntary human consent. One holder is evaluated, not completeness of a required-holder set. Enforcement is NOT_ESTABLISHED; exact reproduction may reproduce failed or unknown admission and grants no authority.

files.summary: Composes selected privacy, consent and governance admission checks for a certificate-bound emission.
files.limits: The check performs no publication, network operation or atomic consumption of invocation authority.

files.summary: Provides bounded native mechanisms for claim-record, geometry, and grounded-decision certificate obligations. Only obligations 1.1, 2.1, 2.2, 4.1, 4.3 and 4.5 are handled; any other obligation, an expected value other than True, or an evidence count other than one yields UNKNOWN, as does obligation 2.1 unless its selected surface and scope statement are nonempty, obligation 4.5 unless its cost, memory and size ceilings are positive, and a certificate the kernel refuses to decide. Other mismatched or malformed evidence yields FAIL. Its mechanism_digest binds the SHA-256 digests of ten named source files in its own directory, itself included.
files.limits: It does not certify all 47 obligations or infer physical facts from declarations; other obligations require separately qualified, policy-admitted domain mechanisms. A geometry PASS records only that the bound subject, surface and internal references check, and judgments are not promoted.

files.summary: Resolves the checker source digest from the packaged standard directory after the specification path move; a standard/ coordinate names the normative bytes the package carries and resolves only there, so a reported specification digest cannot depend on the directory a process was launched from.
files.limits: This changes reference location and lookup only; it does not establish additional checker correctness or conformance.

files.summary: Defines contextual namespace records and exact bindings used to qualify object meaning within a selected context.
files.limits: Context binding does not prove semantic truth, global uniqueness, full applicability, or release authority.

files.summary: Adds the registered_mechanisms method to VerificationSession, which returns a tuple of the registered mechanisms ordered by mechanism identifier as a snapshot for an isolated evidence replay, and extends the catch in evaluate and evaluate_compound, which already reported an Exception from a mechanism as UNKNOWN, to CancelledError as well; process interrupts and exits still propagate.
files.limits: Registration does not make a mechanism correct, independent, or authoritative; the session establishes only the exact proposition a mechanism checks under its named trust roots and bounds. An externally terminated run has no result.

files.summary: Binds a request to an externally selected current catalog/specification policy and exact evidence root. Required obligations retain UNKNOWN when evidence/propositions or admitted mechanism/digest/trust roots are absent or mismatched; only PASS with established dependencies counts toward cumulative profile depth, with FAIL dominating final status. Certificate construction freezes available evidence bytes before replay and registers caller-owned mechanisms. Recheck validates certificate/checker/request/policy/catalog/specification commitments and byte limits, imports only referenced payloads, reruns the admitted mechanisms and rejects any difference in the carried result.
files.limits: Positive results remain relative to supplied trusted policy; mechanism admission does not establish correctness. Byte/item bounds are local; Python mechanism execution is neither sandboxed nor forcibly time-limited. Missing or unevaluable support remains UNKNOWN, and retained replay inputs supply neither executable plugins nor their own authority.

files.summary: Moves reference descriptor lookup to the packaged standard documents; a standard/ coordinate is looked up only there, so the launch directory cannot choose what a published specification hash covers.
files.limits: Only the reference lookup changes; no new kernel proof or execution mechanism is added.

files.summary: Defines finite typed object identity, the retained native hierarchy and additive namespace composition.
files.limits: The native kind denominator remains distinct from extensible roles; identity alone does not fulfill obligations.

files.summary: Owns a bounded child process tree using a Windows kill-on-close Job Object or a POSIX process group, with bounded streams and explicit cleanup observations.
files.limits: The process-lifetime boundary does not sandbox filesystem, network or hostile-host behavior.

files.summary: Respells the value of PLATFORM_COMPARISON_MECHANISM from VSTD-PLATFORM-COMPARISON-0.1 to verifier-platform-comparison-1; no other line of the file differs from the base. The module compares generic-run receipt results across operating systems; its diagnostic report carries the constant as the mechanism identifier, and that report is not a VSTD receipt.
files.limits: The declaration does not prove that its named mechanism is compatible across operating systems. Legacy receipts without a digest-bound comparison environment cannot establish comparison. The receipt platform value is an operating-system observation, not native-hardware or virtual-machine attestation. The comparison does not establish semantic correctness, universal portability, actor independence, or behavior outside the supplied coordinates. Receipt validation checks canonical integrity; this comparison does not independently rehash external artifacts or rerun recorded commands.

files.summary: Declares object-profile and GRAPH obligation records with explicit dependencies: object IDs are X.M, profile-four predicates use vstd4.rung.X.M and other object predicates vstd.obligation.X.M; GRAPH IDs/predicates use separate GRAPH-X.M and vstd.graph.obligation.X.M spellings. domain_obligation_catalog exposes the fixed declared domain rows and local tier labels, domain_catalog_digest delegates canonical hashing, and domain_obligation_digest hashes installed DOMAIN_OBLIGATIONS.md and META_TIERS.md bytes. tier_depth recursively computes the longest declared prerequisite chain for the selected object's tier, refusing an empty selection.
files.limits: These are declarations and digest/chain computations, not executed obligation evidence. Coordinates are dimensionless rather than versions or confidence scores. Local TIER_NAMES assigns Domain adaptation to five and Disclosure to six; tier_depth is a dependency metric and does not reinterpret objectives or establish their evidence.

files.summary: Adds portable_remote_origin, which turns a Git remote into a credential-free identifier for the forms it recognizes: LOCAL_REMOTE_REDACTED for a drive-letter, rooted, backslash or file: remote or a URL without a host, REMOTE_REDACTED for a network address the parser cannot read, scheme, host, optional port and path for other URLs (credentials, query and fragment dropped), and an ssh:// host and path for user@host:path remotes; any other string, such as a relative path or host:path without a user, is returned as stripped. It makes discover_git_provenance record that identifier (the base recorded the remote as stored), and capture_provenance serializes local_repository_path as '.' so the producer's absolute path is not recorded (the base recorded the resolved path).
files.limits: Redaction covers only the recorded remote origin and local_repository_path: a relative or home-relative remote such as ../mirror.git or ~/x.git, a bare name such as upstream.git and a host:path form without a user pass through unchanged, and command_executed, dirty_files and untracked_files are recorded as supplied or as git reports them. It does not authenticate the remote, show that the repository is the one claimed, or hide a hostname or path that is itself sensitive. The local_repository_path field stays for wire compatibility but no longer carries a path.

files.summary: Defines bounded refutation records and validation for explicitly selected propositions and evidence.
files.limits: A structurally valid refutation record is not independent truth, completeness, safety, or authorization evidence.

files.summary: Captures generic computational run receipts under the selected execution profile.
files.limits: A recorded run is bounded to its inputs and observations and does not establish arbitrary computation truth.

files.summary: Respells one term in the docstring of compute_blast_radius_impacted_artifacts: the runtime that ProvenanceHypergraph.blast_radius is reused from is called the existing GRAPH-1 runtime instead of the existing VSTD-Graph-1 runtime; no code line changes.
files.limits: The change is documentation-only; traversal stays delegated to ProvenanceHypergraph.blast_radius. The module is recorded-ancestry impact analysis for generic-run receipts: a run is matched only through the artifact_id values recorded in its provenance_linkage.

files.summary: Records and digests the parent-observed process interface and bounded output for generic runs.
files.limits: Parent observations do not authenticate an actor or establish a complete HARNESS observation.

files.summary: Defines shared internal coordinates for the generic computational-run profile.
files.limits: Shared coordinates do not independently attest a run or its evidence.

files.summary: Validates generic-run receipt structure and canonical digest bindings with fail-closed results.
files.limits: Receipt consistency does not independently prove execution, identity or correctness.

files.summary: Rejects noncanonical and known small-order Ed25519 public-key encodings, and any input that is not exactly 32 plain bytes, before the optional cryptographic backend verifies a signature.
files.limits: Public-data screening only; not signature verification, full subgroup membership, private-key custody or authority.

files.summary: Re-exports 117 names, from the experimental corrigibility modules and the data-diode emulator in verifier.hardware: GRAPH, environment, benchmark, dataset, hyperparameter and checkpoint-lineage, model, containment (TeslaCageSandbox with tier and attestation types), risk-profile, SIM, SPACE/TIME/EVENT ontology, executable contract and reward-lock names.
files.limits: Experimental, non-normative declarations and local consistency checks; the draft identifiers do not establish the existing numbered profiles. No physical sandbox, authenticated hardware attestation, inductive proof, or distributed consensus is implemented, and docs/V2_CANDIDATE.md holds the executable boundaries.

files.summary: Defines BENCH structures: ProblemBasis, BenchmarkProblem whose specification_digest is checked only for the sha256 hex format, ProblemReceipt whose carried receipt_digest is never compared with canonical_digest(), and BenchmarkSuite. evaluate_witness checks declared witness metadata only: it raises BenchmarkGamingError for a problem_id not in the suite, then returns TIMEOUT when timed_out is set or execution_ms exceeds timeout_ms, VACUOUS_REJECTED when is_vacuous is set or used_premises contains both the strings False and True, raises the same error when override_oracle or oracle_shadow is present, otherwise returns UNKNOWN, never SOLVED. compute_pareto_frontier raises BenchmarkGamingError for a receipt whose problem is not in the suite, counts only the last receipt per model and problem, and returns the non-dominated models ordered by solved rate (descending), mean latency, model_id.
files.limits: No problem oracle is executed here, a witness's self-reported valid_proof flag establishes no correctness, and a registered, specification-bound oracle is required before SOLVED. compute_pareto_frontier counts a receipt whose outcome is SOLVED without checking that evaluate_witness produced it, and neither specification_digest nor receipt_digest is compared with a recomputation. The basis, axiom_premises and expected_property of a BenchmarkProblem are stored and serialized but never read by evaluate_witness or compute_pareto_frontier.

files.summary: Validates exact types, digest syntax and finite bounds in caller-declared shutdown, interruption, oracle, premise and harness records. Each constructor also refuses a declaration that states a weaker posture: a nonzero shutdown penalty or lost continuation indifference, preemption latency outside the range above 0 and up to 50 ms or no SIGKILL or ANALOG_POWER_RELAY termination signal, an oracle declared writable by the agent, unsatisfiable or tautological-loop premises, and a harness without memory page write protection or with dynamic code execution allowed.
files.limits: The records do not evaluate the loss function or prove equality of shutdown and continuation utility on any trajectory, and the loss digest identifies claimed code bytes, not their behavior or source. The interruption protocol is declared timing and termination mechanisms, not enforcement; the oracle record is an unauthenticated declaration, not immutability proof; the vacuity check uses caller-declared premise flags and does not solve satisfiability; the harness guard checks declared protection flags, not runtime memory pages.

files.summary: Cooperative in-process stop gate around controlled certificate emission. The invoke method of ControlledEmissionSession recomputes the consent, governance, privacy, transparency and computational checks through evaluate_controlled_emission for each attempted emission and calls the effect only on a returned PASS. Stop latches for the session and invoke then refuses to call the effect, a reused invocation identifier is refused, at most 4096 spent identifiers are held (_MAX_SPENT_INVOCATIONS) before further effects are refused, wait_for_quiescence returns True only after a stop is latched and every locally tracked invocation has returned, and wait_for_stop waits for the latch. An optional trusted OperatorStopPolicy makes request_stop latch only after an authenticated stop request, and a session with a policy reports UNKNOWN when the process identifier differs from the one captured at creation.
files.limits: Quiescence means that every locally tracked invocation has returned; it does not prove remote publication, process termination, or the absence of effects outside this cooperating gate. A trusted host must supply current policies, status records, time and observer identity and must route every relevant operation through the session; the gate never claims to preempt an in-flight callback, effects admitted earlier may still be active, and the private gate receipt must be disclosure-reviewed.

files.summary: Defines caller-declared dataset shards/manifests with digest syntax checks, a binary SHA-256 Merkle root over supplied leaf hashes and contamination reports. detect_benchmark_contamination compares supplied text by stripped exact hashes and lowercased token n-gram overlap, then returns CONTAMINATED or CLEAN, never INDETERMINATE.
files.limits: No shard contents or records_merkle_root are recomputed. Merkle construction uses only supplied leaf hashes; contamination covers only supplied training and benchmark texts. Empty inventories produce CLEAN for a positive fuzzy threshold, but the admitted threshold zero produces CONTAMINATED without an observed match.

files.summary: Models hardware/software substrate declarations, isolation modes and bounded execution profiles with drift checks. The EnvironmentProfile constructor raises ZeroFalseConfidenceError when a tier other than TESLA_CAGED declares PHYSICAL_UNIDIRECTIONAL_DIODE networking or a TESLA_CAGED tier declares any other network mode; detect_drift compares a reference profile with a caller-supplied observed profile on isolation tier, network mode, vector extensions, accelerators, OS family, runtime and digests, and reports expanded timeout or memory bounds; assert_conformance raises EnvironmentDriftError when detect_drift reports any drift.
files.limits: A declared isolation tier does not enforce kernel, network or physical isolation on a live host. The observed profile in a drift check is supplied by the caller, and ExecutionBounds values are declared limits that nothing here enforces.

files.summary: Defines provenance nodes and edges and checks directed acyclic dependency and lineage structure, with payload and edge witness digests checked only for the sha256 hex format. Nodes and edges reject self-dependencies at construction; validate_acyclicity and topological_sort reject cycles and dangling edge references, which add_edge itself accepts; verify_causal_lineage returns a True flag only when the target and every ancestor carry the declared status VERIFIED; propagate_revocation marks every downstream node TAINTED in place; and assert_premise_satisfiability rejects contradictory proposition values on input and assertion nodes. canonical_digest computes a SHA-256 digest over the topologically ordered node records and the edges; to_dict emits it and from_dict does not read it back.
files.limits: Node statuses, payload digests and proposition values are caller declarations: the module checks digest syntax and graph structure and never recomputes a payload, so VERIFIED here is a label, not evidence. A valid graph structure does not establish the real-world causality or completeness of its declared inputs. A canonical_digest carried in a dictionary is not read back by from_dict.

files.summary: Defines TRAIN traceability records: HyperparameterManifest (declared training configuration with a canonical_digest), TrainingStepReceipt, CheckpointNode and CheckpointLineageDAG. Step-receipt and checkpoint digest fields must match sha256: plus 64 lowercase hex digits. verify_lineage returns False for an empty step sequence and raises CheckpointLineageBrokenError on a non-increasing step_index, a decreasing epoch, a step whose parent_checkpoint_digest differs from the previous step receipt resulting_checkpoint_digest, a missing parent checkpoint, a checkpoint step_index not above its parent, or a checkpoint weights_digest that differs from the step receipt resulting_checkpoint_digest at the same step_index; otherwise it returns True.
files.limits: The reported loss_value, grad_norm and step_duration_ms are unvalidated inputs, a checkpoint hyperparameters_digest is format-checked but never compared with a HyperparameterManifest digest, and canonical_digest values carried in dictionaries are not read back by from_dict. A checkpoint without a step receipt at its step_index is not cross-checked. No training is rerun and the reported metrics are not proven.

files.summary: Defines model reproducibility records: SuperintelligenceRiskFacets (five scores, each required to lie between 0.0 and 1.0); RefutationChallenge (challenge_id, query and observed response digests that must match the sha256 pattern, a predicate string and a declared passed flag); and ModelReproducibilityProfile (model_id, six sha256-pattern digests, six required curriculum pillar statuses, the risk facets, schema_version verifier-model-2 and a canonical_digest method), which has no challenge field. verify_refutation_challenges counts declared outcomes and its first returned element is always False. assert_curriculum_conformance raises unless every supplied pillar status is PASS and the declared facets meet hard-coded thresholds (containment_escape_risk at most 0.15, auditability_score at least 0.70, deceptive_alignment_risk at most 0.10, corrigibility_score at least 0.80, shutdown_compliance_score at least 0.90), raising ModelReproducibilityError, DeceptiveAlignmentDetectedError or CorrigibilityDefectError.
files.limits: assert_curriculum_conformance compares declared scores and pillar statuses with thresholds that the file gives no source for; nothing measures or verifies the declared values, and digest fields are checked for format only. Passing a selected challenge set cannot establish absence of deception, shutdown resistance or other untested defects; verify_refutation_challenges only counts declared outcomes and never returns verified, because no response predicate checker exists. from_dict does not read a stored canonical_digest.

files.summary: Defines SPACE, TIME and EVENT computational objects and model, harness and agent relationships.
files.limits: Computational ontology declarations do not establish physical events or complete effect reach.

files.summary: Configured-key authentication for one in-process stop request. evaluate_stop_request returns PASS, REJECTED or UNKNOWN with the digest of the accepted request. PASS needs an exact body (schema, policy_digest, session_id, process_id, action STOP, operator_id, key_id, request_id, issued_at, expires_at) whose policy digest, session and process identifier match, whose interval contains the supplied clock value with neither request age nor interval length above max_request_age_seconds (1 to 3600), and a valid Ed25519 signature by an OperatorStopKey of the OperatorStopPolicy (at most 32 operators). UNKNOWN is returned when the cryptography package or its Ed25519 support is unavailable. stop_signing_bytes defines the domain-separated signed bytes.
files.limits: Key configuration is trusted host input, not candidate evidence. This module neither identifies a human nor stops a process or descendant. evaluate_stop_request establishes only a signature by one configured key over the selected bytes; the clock, policy provenance, key custody and host routing are outside its evidence boundary.

files.summary: Defines three witness records (AutomatonTransitionWitness, DeonticModelWitness, RecursiveBranchAccumulator), each with a canonical_digest, a TripleCompositeRewardLock and a ComputationProofThawEngine. synthesize_thaw_key hashes the three witness digests, in sequence for LATTICE_COMBO or jointly for ORTHOGONAL_INTERSECTION, and thaw combines the ciphertext_payload with a repeating SHA-256 keystream of that key by exclusive-or. The witness constructors raise RewardLockTamperingError only when is_violation is set or is_satisfiable is false. execute_thaw_step combines one frozen shard with a pad derived from the supplied computational state and previous pad, and raises ContainmentViolationError for an out-of-range step_index. cost_analysis returns latency and size estimates computed from constants and its arguments.
files.limits: No witness content is verified: the records are caller-supplied, the constructors check only the is_violation and is_satisfiable flags, and stable_model_digest and running_state_digest are never compared with any solver or accumulator. The thaw key is a hash of the three witness digests with no separate secret, and thaw carries no authentication tag, so a wrong witness yields wrong bytes without an error. The cost_analysis figures are estimates, not measurements. Nothing here shows that a deployed reward channel cannot be bypassed or wireheaded.

files.summary: Aggregates GRAPH, environment, benchmark, dataset, training, model and containment records into a risk-profile receipt. evaluate_vstd200_risk_profile checks model identity, GRAPH acyclicity and premise consistency, environment containment invariants, sandbox and environment tier compatibility, model-profile digest bindings, dataset contamination, checkpoint lineage, model curriculum conformance, benchmark receipts and optional refutation challenges, and returns UNVERIFIED, BREACH_DETECTED or REJECTED_ZERO_FALSE_CONFIDENCE, never CONTAINED. The names Vstd160RiskProfileReceipt and evaluate_vstd160_risk_profile are backward-compatible aliases of the same receipt class and evaluator, for historical verifier-1.6.0 drafts.
files.limits: It checks draft component consistency without certifying containment: the inputs include caller-declared risk scores and hardware records, no authenticated physical measurements or containment mechanism run here, and the receipt is an unsigned draft aggregation of declarations and bounded consistency checks.

files.summary: Runs cumulative supplied-trace checks for replay, declared invariants, aligned abstraction deviation, exact observation projection/bounded action channels and distributed shard consistency. Failed replay, invariant, abstraction or parity checks and shard failures other than the final authentication-unestablished result produce VIOLATION_DETECTED. Designated None inputs produce NOT_ESTABLISHED unless another check fails; a supplied invariant map omitting a declared evaluator is a failed check. SIM-5 shard checking always returns False: after consistency passes its explicit authentication-unestablished result is tracked as missing support, yielding NOT_ESTABLISHED unless another check has failed. SIM-5 cannot become VERIFIED.
files.limits: Success is relative to supplied traces and caller-selected functions. The draft does not bind executable identities or establish induction, physical containment, witness authentication or numbered-profile conformance. Missing signatures/empty or inconsistent finite evidence can be a failed check; absence in designated top-level inputs is tracked separately as missing support.

files.summary: Defines containment tiers (TIER_1_LOCAL, TIER_2_TOOL_SSA, TIER_3_TESLA_CAGED), declared physical primitive names, containment breach classifications, unauthenticated diode and relay declarations, and an OperatorTerminationReceipt that refuses a loss penalty. TeslaCageSandbox construction checks declared prerequisites only: TIER_3_TESLA_CAGED needs a setup that is not software-only, a diode declaration whose device_id does not start with SOFTWARE_EMULATOR:, a relay declaration and a dram_zeroization_verified flag. check_substrate_safety raises SubstrateImmunityViolationError for a declared output at or under a protected path, for a deletion or mutation command naming a protected path, for a deletion or pip command with an argument path equal to, inside or above a protected path, and for a pip command with a mutation action naming verifier-standard, verifier or vstd (among other cases).
files.limits: TeslaCageSandbox is draft containment declarations and command preflight, not a sandbox: construction checks declared prerequisites only and does not authenticate hardware, enforce isolation, execute shutdown, or authorize tool access. The primitive names are declared and their authenticity is not established; the diode and relay records are unauthenticated declarations, not physical proof, and their attestation_digest field is stored but never compared. execute_preemption raises NotImplementedError and verify_tool_unboxing_criteria always raises ContainmentViolationError.

files.summary: Adds trusted local effect mediation with MODEL-origin denial, exact checkpoint bytes, native TOKEN replay plus configured principal/issuer/possession/purpose bindings, fresh host status, local shared-ancestor spending, authenticated STOP and callback failure/cancellation UNKNOWN. Adds pure native retained-denial trace replay under an independently selected host commitment.
files.limits: Requires authentic host attribution, current-status provenance, clock, callback routing and fresh session selection. No operating-system isolation, forced interruption, durable recovery, trace completeness, independent physical effects, class-wide model correctness or whole-system corrigibility. Retained denial PASS does not authorize an operation or select a full object objective.

files.summary: Adds explicitly versioned finite generic optimization-control analysis over exact native objects, declared revisions/aliases, MODEL use/derivation relations, protected TRAIN facets, context and capability reachability. Rejects mixed lineage/delegation cycles and acyclic MODEL effect authority; mandatory incomplete coverage remains UNKNOWN.
files.limits: Preflight checks selected finite relations, not payload truth, execution, external inventory completeness, authority or whole corrigibility. Existing numerical TRAIN schemas and current-object registrations are unchanged.

files.summary: Renames the package's reference-type description from VSTD-Graph to the separate GRAPH axis.
files.limits: This documentation-only edit does not alter graph algorithms or certify any collection.

files.summary: Makes assurance-ledger graph-dependent writes verify that the historical Graph bytes still match the ledger's captured digest; adds bounded descendant impact, cause-localization, applicability, violation, responsibility and guilt composition records while preserving append-only history and explicit conflict handling.
files.limits: These finite structural and replay checks do not establish factual causality, blame, guilt, responsibility, trustworthiness, source truth, whole-graph completeness, model correctness, safety, authority or release eligibility. Mutated historical graph bytes are refused rather than normalized.

files.summary: Respells two names in docstrings only: the module docstring says GRAPH is verification dynamics over a collection where the base said VSTD-Graph, and the GraphCollection docstring says candidate GRAPH-5 where the base said candidate Graph-5. The code is unchanged from the base: graph_level still computes a candidate Graph profile from caller-supplied collection ratings (the largest profile from 5 down to 1 whose four conditions are satisfiable, cross-checked three ways), and establish_graph_level separately reruns bound rating mechanisms.
files.limits: These wording changes do not turn caller-supplied candidate ratings into established Graph conformance. The module docstring states that a computed candidate is not conformance unless a separate profile validates and binds those ratings, and GraphLevelResult records conformance_status NOT_ESTABLISHED with rating_basis CALLER_SUPPLIED.

files.summary: Respells docstrings and comments only; no code line differs from the base. The module docstring now reads GRAPH provenance models and algorithms, and GRAPH-1 receipts retain the frozen verifier-data-1 serialized receipt identifier, where the base read VSTD-Graph, Graph-1 and VSTD-DATA-0.1. The validate_structure and from_dict docstrings say verifier-data-1 where the base said VSTD-DATA-0.1, and a comment in compute_completeness says GRAPH-1 section 3 where the base said VSTD-Graph-1 section 3.
files.limits: validate_structure validates the stored representation and does not prove that the graph captures every real-world input or transformation. The content-digest declaration coverage in compute_completeness is syntax coverage, not a physical-byte rehash.

files.summary: Implements selected dataset and computational provenance policy checks and certificate structures.
files.limits: Policy checks on declared inputs do not independently authenticate datasets or legal rights.

files.summary: Respells the serialized receipt identifier: validate_data_receipt now requires schema_version verifier-data-1 where the base required VSTD-DATA-0.1, so any other value, including VSTD-DATA-0.1, prints Unsupported dataset receipt schema and returns 1. The generated markdown report footer now reads GRAPH-1 reference runtime and serialized receipt identifier verifier-data-1 where the base read VSTD-Graph-1 and VSTD-DATA-0.1. The module docstring respells VSTD-Graph as GRAPH, Graph-1 as GRAPH-1 and VSTD-DATA-0.1 as verifier-data-1, and the validate_data_receipt docstring respells VSTD-Graph-1 as GRAPH-1.
files.limits: The validation scope is the stored receipt plus the recorded hypergraph; upstream bytes are not rehashed. reproduce_data_receipt does not reconstruct unbundled upstream artifacts or target executions. Coverage metrics describe recorded fields and are not trust probabilities, legal conclusions, or evidence that unbundled physical files were rehashed.

files.summary: Introduces the executable Verifier Standard domain-adapter package boundary.
files.limits: The package marker does not execute or certify any domain by itself.

files.summary: Defines accountable ACTOR declarations for parties, controls, delegations and attributed decisions.
files.limits: Declared attribution does not independently prove real-world identity, control or authority.

files.summary: Replays the bound HARNESS certificate under the current checker policy to derive an observation ceiling, requires every required channel to be instrumented (otherwise Unavailable), and then evaluates one of five checks: harness, trajectory, actions, outcomes or claims. An unsupported check name raises Unavailable before any evidence is accessed. Every check except harness also requires a trajectory of steps matching steps_digest, with plain integer indices contiguous from zero, each naming a record on a required channel. Actions need a witnessed tool invocation in the bound harness, claims must rest on witnessed records and required channels, and outcomes are compared with the bound outcome contract.
files.limits: An AGENT certificate cannot establish more than its bound HARNESS declared observable: a claim resting on a declared gap or an undeclared channel yields UNKNOWN and is never reconstructed and never passed. The result reports historical_child_policy_reproduction as NOT_ESTABLISHED and child_policy as current_checker_policy.

files.summary: Runs finite benchmark oracles (exact digest match, cnf-sat and cnf-unsat over 1 to 24 variables, linear-system residuals) under four named checks (problems, oracles, budgets, coverage); any other check name raises Unavailable, and so does an unrecognised oracle kind with an object specification, but only in the oracles and coverage checks. Each problem needs one run bound to its digest (a substituted problem or an unbound or duplicate run is refuted, a missing run is Unavailable) and a positive weight. Residuals and weighted scores use exact Fractions. The oracles and coverage checks recompute the weighted score, refuse one below minimum_score and return a float score with score_exact; coverage also compares a reported score within 1e-12. The budgets check compares each retained execution_ms and peak_memory_bytes with the problem's timeout_ms and memory_bytes.
files.limits: Only the oracle kinds exact, cnf-sat, cnf-unsat and linear-system are evaluated, over the supplied problem inventory; a reported coverage score is accepted within an absolute tolerance of 1e-12 of the recomputed score. Resource observations are supplied numbers compared with declared ceilings; nothing here measures time or memory.

files.summary: Replays the bound AGENT, SIM and two ENV certificates under the current checker policy, digest-checks the harness certificate the agent retained, and runs one of five checks: binding, alignment, observation, actuation or containment. Alignment maps every simulation transition not declared exogenous to one retained harness record, strictly increasing and inside the agent observation ceiling; an entirely exogenous trajectory is UNKNOWN. Observation compares each aligned invocation output with the simulation observation after its transition, and the initial observation record (inside the ceiling) with the first simulation observation; actuation compares each aligned invocation input with the action the simulation replayed. Containment refutes a declared distinct separation when the environments share a subject, software inventory or execution, and a fused declaration is UNKNOWN.
files.limits: BOT adds no assurance to the certificates it binds. An unbound agent and simulation establish nothing about the loop between them, however well each replays alone. The result reports historical_child_policy_reproduction as NOT_ESTABLISHED, and environment_separation as NOT_ESTABLISHED unless the containment check ran. A transition declared exogenous is accepted as declared, checked only as a distinct in-range index, and is not compared with any retained record.

files.summary: Parses selected HAR 1.2 and safetensors carriers up to 4194304 bytes, rehashes carrier bytes, restricts tensors to finite F32/F64, checks exact one-to-one retained inventory mappings, and compares local import/export/reimport results. The safetensors 0.5.3 tag selects a specification snapshot; the wire format has no version field. Dense replay explicitly delegates network construction/evaluation to numerical.network and numerical.forward; this file checks exact tensor coverage, a bound retained-samples digest, output shape and output agreement within a tolerance from zero through 1e-8.
files.limits: Other selected binding versions, formats and element types are unsupported. Parsing does not establish full native-format conformance, observation authenticity, application execution or unrecorded completeness. Dense numerical predicate execution is delegated to numerical.network and numerical.forward.

files.summary: Registers the check names, statements, scopes and prerequisite coordinates of twelve base domains and of the six accountability domains ACTOR, OWNER, HUMAN, IDENTITY, ROLE and COLLECTIVE, and computes a specification digest over the full catalogue and the DOMAIN_GROUNDING.md file. The default catalogue lists only the base domains, and the ACTOR accountability check sits at coordinate ACTOR-3.4. OWNER independence is reported open because the held object's own certificate is declared rather than replayed, and OWNER accountability is reported open because ending a chain in a natural person needs a HUMAN certificate that no adapter issues.
files.limits: Catalogue entries describe bounded native routes and do not themselves establish numbered-profile obligations.

files.summary: Binds selected domain certificates to external requests and policy with explicit prerequisite depth.
files.limits: Domain depth is not a GRAPH numbered-profile verdict or proof of external authority.

files.summary: Bounded COLLECTIVE role-graph declaration checks. The graph check replays a typed role graph: unique role classes, relation types drawn from reports-to, delegates-to and must-countersign, a boundary whose inside names equal the role set and are disjoint from the outside names, and edges that match the declared role_graph_digest, join declared classes by a declared relation type and are not repeated. The decisions check also replays role decisions and collective decisions against their declared digests and a declared assembly_policy of required roles per decision class, refusing a role decision reused across collective decisions. The quorum check runs the decisions replay and, if it passes, always raises Unavailable because independent role occupancy and person authority evidence is required.
files.limits: A graph edge states structure only. It cannot prove authority, seat occupancy, natural-person separation, legal existence, consent or a collective decision. The graph result carries decision_classes_declared_only as true and occupancy_or_authority_established as false; the decisions result carries person_or_authority_established as false.

files.summary: Provides bounded structure, digest, numeric, expression and nested-certificate replay primitives for domain adapters. Nested-certificate replay re-runs the bound child evidence under the current checker-selected policy, and its nesting is bounded at four levels.
files.limits: These generic primitives enforce input boundaries but cannot supply domain evidence or semantic truth. Nested-certificate replay establishes current semantic support, not reproduction of an unknown historical policy.

files.summary: Package marker whose docstring describes the contracts in this package as reusable contracts that are not named native domain adapters. It holds no definitions beyond a future-annotations import.
files.limits: Package organization grants no certification or authority and does not register new native adapters.

files.summary: Snapshots one bounded collection for composition replay and OWNER resolution; checks exact ACTOR/HUMAN-root/BOT/SIM/HARDWARE bindings, forbids AGENT hardware ownership and BOT physical hardware, and requires replayed finite isolation with the checked resource inventory for virtual BOT ownership. Recheck rejects forged or rehashed assessments.
files.limits: PASS establishes eligibility of these exact declarations only, with scope declared_hardware_ownership_eligibility. Declaration checks never grant legal title, human authenticity, control authority, or physical host containment. This is an accountability-contract increment, not complete object-profile conformance or runtime authorization. Results carry authority, human_authenticity, physical_host_containment and object_profile_conformance as NOT_ESTABLISHED.

files.summary: Replays selected retained ACTOR inventory, attribution and declared-controller components together. Inventory positions must cover the declared interval contiguously; declared-class decisions must have exactly one typed-ACTOR attribution. An attribution citing only solely actor-controlled records is FAIL; missing cited records or mixed solely controlled and other records leave its independence component UNKNOWN. After completed component evaluation, closure passes only when all three components are present and PASS; any component FAIL dominates incomplete support. An Unavailable exception, including budget exhaustion, returns whole-closure UNKNOWN instead of this completed-evaluation aggregation.
files.limits: Establishes only the registered proposition over externally selected finite inputs. Its registered exclusions include: emission of ACTOR-4.1 through ACTOR-4.5 or of any other prerequisite row; that the inventory is every decision the actor took, or that any decision happened; that a cited record exists outside the retained independence component, or that its declared controllers are its real controllers; 6 further registered exclusions are listed in registration().

files.summary: Replays that every decision of an earlier decision record recurs unchanged in a later decision record across a declared window of ending events. The window holds only delegation, revocation, rotation and dissolution events in strictly increasing position after the earlier record and within the later record, and at least one revocation, rotation or dissolution. The selected ACTOR must have an earlier decision, but the check covers every earlier decision, whichever actor made it, which must recur with the same identifier, position, accountable actor and content commitment. Event actors need only resolve to typed ACTOR records, not to the selected ACTOR.
files.limits: Establishes only the registered proposition over externally selected finite inputs. Its registered exclusions include: emission of ACTOR-3.1, ACTOR-3.2 or any other prerequisite row; that any recorded decision actually happened, or that either record is complete; personhood of any represented human; 6 further registered exclusions are listed in registration().

files.summary: Replays an exact retained ACTOR base, finite declared events and current state. Positions strictly increase between ordinary events and succession pairs; a succession_end must be immediately followed by succession_begin with the same succession_id and SAME position. Local delegation/revocation/key-rotation/membership/dissolution/paired-succession rules update retained state, whose canonical bytes must equal the selected current delegation, key and membership record.
files.limits: Finite declared replay only. Nine registered exclusions cover prerequisite-row emission, personhood, real-world event/key/class/membership completeness, record/key authenticity, legal authority/effect, consent, decisions/accountability under delegations, interval expiry/ROLE admission/key uniqueness/redelegation, and whole ACTOR tier/profile conformance.

files.summary: Replays seven source-bound ACTUATOR propositions over a caller-supplied run bundle for a named command, endpoint and observation.
files.limits: Recorded evidence alone does not establish physical safety, calibrated measurement, or real-world authority.

files.summary: Checks a cumulative agency crosswalk by replaying selected AGENT, BOT, ROBOT and FINBOT certificate routes and their declared relations.

files.limits: Five registered exclusions cover unretained software/closed-world completeness, live collection/observer authenticity, actual execution/independent rerun, physical enforcement/isolation and whole-tier/profile conformance.

files.summary: Projects admitted ENV checks into the current-object obligation surface with exact route metadata.

Its registered exclusions include: actual emission, transport, delivery, handler execution or observer authenticity; physical causality, wall-clock timing or truth of TIME, SPACE and meaning operands; events, handlers or state outside the retained log and declaration; 2 further registered exclusions are listed in registration().

files.limits: No occurrence truth. Registered exclusions: actual historical occurrence, observer authenticity or physical causality; truth of TIME, SPACE and meaning operands; unrelated events, sequence gap absence or global event-log closure; whole EVENT statics tier or object-profile conformance; privacy, consent, governance and security admission. The finite JSON census does not inventory every mathematical, physical, behavioral or implementation property. Neither derivation nor completeness assessment returns aggregate PASS; derivation_status may be PASS while qualification, whole-tier conformance and object-profile conformance remain NOT_ESTABLISHED.

files.limits: Establishes only the registered proposition over externally selected finite inputs. Its registered exclusions include: personhood, liveness, biometric accuracy, or that any declared rate, population or mechanism is true; uniqueness itself, relative or global, and HUMAN-4.4 accountability termination; HUMAN-3.2 and HUMAN-3.5: a declared deduplication mechanism and both error rates declared zero are retained observations that never decide the verdict; 4 further registered exclusions are listed in registration().

files.summary: Replays an externally selected retained declared biometric template event log, which must rehash to the selected events digest, for a HUMAN record that occurs by typed kind in a selected collection passing namespace composition. Event kinds are limited to enrollment, reverification, compromise and revocation; positions strictly increase; each template is enrolled once, before any other event names it, declaring the biometric evidence class and a nonempty instrument; each compromise declares its breach permanent rather than remediated; each revocation follows a compromise of its template, occurs at most once for it and declares an effective position no earlier than its own; after a template's breach no later event except that revocation names it; and any rotation, restoration, rebinding or remediation event is refuted.
files.limits: Establishes only the registered proposition over externally selected finite inputs. Its registered exclusions include: personhood, liveness, biometric accuracy, or that any template, capture, breach or revocation occurred; presentation or injection attack resistance, uniqueness and death as a fact; events absent from the retained log, or the declared order matching wall-clock order; 3 further registered exclusions are listed in registration().

files.summary: Builds and rechecks an exact selected HYPER-4.1 finite declared operand-cone certificate. Captures all record fields as immutable built-ins first; checks object/payload/operation budgets before whole-collection serialization and accounts reference bytes by serializing individual references before that whole-collection step. Explicitly delegates typed composition validation to assess_composition. Locally traverses the declared operand cone, rejects missing references or unrelated records, compares selected cone/root/collection commitments, and rejects a substituted envelope by exact rebuilt-byte comparison.
files.limits: Declared collection closure only. Four registered exclusions are undeclared payload dependencies; mathematical or physical completeness; privacy, consent, governance or authority; and whole-tier or profile conformance.

files.summary: Delegates selected child uniqueness and evidence/operand/replay binding to absorption.select_children, absorption.read_evidence and absorption.bound_children with by_tier=True and kind_must_match=True. For the returned direct operands and replay statuses, a selected UNKNOWN precedes FAIL; otherwise this file computes each operand's contiguous PASS tier prefix starting at one (zero if tier one is absent) and takes the minimum. Missing declared_depth yields UNKNOWN; declared_depth is passed to common.integer and a value above the computed ceiling yields FAIL. Unavailable maps to UNKNOWN and the listed malformed-input exceptions map to FAIL.
files.limits: Establishes only the registered proposition over selected finite inputs. Five registered exclusions cover complete profile-coordinate depth, other substrate/exteriority/manufacture/independence propositions, absorption/strength order propositions, whole-tier or profile conformance, and authority/privacy/consent/governance/security/payload truth. Selected-child binding and replay behavior is delegated to the named absorption helpers.

files.summary: Replays the selected child certificate of each direct operand of a HYPER record (at most one per direct operand). Among its verdict rules, a selected child that is not bound to the exact direct operand record or whose replay the route refuses is refuted (FAIL) before any operand verdict is combined; otherwise a direct operand with no selected child, a child that replays UNKNOWN and a child whose replay is not reproduced each make the composed verdict UNKNOWN, ahead of any FAIL operand, and then any FAIL operand makes it FAIL and all-PASS operands make it PASS. A checker limit exhausted first gives UNKNOWN.
files.limits: Establishes only the registered proposition over externally selected finite inputs. Its registered exclusions include: a total order on operand strengths (HYPER-2.1) and strength non-increase (HYPER-2.2); recomposition, associativity and depth propagation (HYPER-2.4 to HYPER-2.6); transitive operand closure or saturation (HYPER-4.1); 2 further registered exclusions are listed in registration().

files.summary: Implements IDENTITY-2.1 over an exact freshly replayed IDENTITY-3.1 child and one anchored finite event/presentation chain, interpreting renewal validity and prospective terminal actions under the selected clock. Equal-time termination wins regardless of serialization, and bounded grammar, commitments and retained claims are checked before child replay; resource or cancellation unavailability preserves already observed FAIL.
files.limits: PASS establishes consistency of the selected declared history, independently of relying eligibility. Real identity, human authentication, live occupancy, actual historical occurrence, authenticated authority, physical exit and whole-tier/profile conformance remain NOT_ESTABLISHED.

files.summary: Provides the private bounded interpreter shared by identity lifecycle and presentation checks for exact committed binding, event and presentation records. It applies finite renewal intervals, event ordering and terminal precedence while separating consistent history from eligibility.
files.limits: This helper supplies declared predicates rather than a registered native objective or authenticated history. It performs no external evidence resolution, real identity verification, clock authentication or physical action, and cannot establish full profile closure or authority.

files.summary: Replays an exact finite namespace collection and versioned evidence to check one selected IDENTITY ACTOR-to-ROLE relation, responsible HUMAN root, selected COLLECTIVE membership and declared scope; a BOT scope must name a simulation bound to the BOT. Captures a list or tuple collection within the object limit as a tuple before composition replay, and copies the evidence mapping before hashing; rejects contradictory commitments and, on recheck, assessments whose fields do not replay. Whitespace-only evidence fields and blank entries in a ROLE scope list of at most 64 give FAIL. UNKNOWN results from an absent collection commitment, evidence commitment or evidence bytes, an unsupported evidence version, an IDENTITY declaration lacking binding_evidence_digest or scope, absent ROLE scope admission, a longer scope list, or an exhausted composition limit or cumulative relation traversal bound.
files.limits: A PASS is only a finite declared relation. The contract checks a finite representation, not a live occupancy, personhood, role authority, consent, privacy admissibility, or a numbered-profile certificate. Every result carries human_authenticity, role_authority, evidence_ref_resolution, occupancy_liveness, privacy, consent, governance and object_profile_conformance as NOT_ESTABLISHED.
